# Concurrency (Workers)

> Part of the [Implementation Status](README.md) index. Real OS threads and cross-thread messaging.

**Coverage**: 4/4 (100%) · **Strict Coverage**: 0/4 (0%).

Format: [Status page format](README.md#status-page-format).

| Feature | Status | Caveats | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Worker` | ✅ | • One listener per event, arrow-function literals only<br>• One message type per direction, declared by annotation<br>• Payloads: structured-clone-safe values only (plus `SharedArrayBuffer`/`MessagePort`, which cross by reference — [ADR-00308](../adr/ADR-00308.md)/[ADR-00309](../adr/ADR-00309.md)); strings share their buffer across threads; no arrays through `onmessage`/`e.data`<br>• `'error'` carries the message string, not an Error object; no `self.onerror`<br>• `terminate()` is cooperative, keeps queued messages, always exits 1<br>• Worker path must be a string literal; a worker module can't also be imported, can't spawn workers, and its named functions can't read its own top-level bindings<br>• `-mm=manual` leaks per message; no combining with `http.listen({workers:N})` | • Two surfaces: Node `worker_threads` and the browser `Worker`/`onmessage` shape ([TDD-00098](../tdd/TDD-00098.md), [ADR-00305](../adr/ADR-00305.md), [ADR-00306](../adr/ADR-00306.md))<br>• The worker file compiles into the same binary as its own entry function<br>• Each thread runs its own event loop (runtime singletons are `thread_local`); messages travel over pipes as pointer envelopes, deep-copied at the boundary<br>• `-mm=gc` registers each thread with Boehm<br>• Uncaught worker exception → `'error'` + `'exit'(1)` on the parent, or process exit if unhandled<br>• darwin/arm64 and Linux (glibc/arm64, Docker) both verified across the whole worker suite, including `-mm=gc` ([ADR-00351](../adr/ADR-00351.md)). `--static` + `-pthread` recheck still pending |
| `BroadcastChannel` | ✅ | • Channel name must be a string literal; one message type per channel name, program-wide (first `postMessage` or annotated `onmessage` fixes it)<br>• `onmessage` property only (arrow-function literal, `(e: { data: T })`); no `addEventListener`, no `'messageerror'`<br>• Array payloads not supported through `onmessage`<br>• `close()` leaks the endpoint's two pipe fds by design (closes a race against an in-flight post)<br>• `-mm=manual` leaks per delivery (payload ownership passes to the listener) | • Process-wide name-keyed registry; each subscriber gets its own deep copy (codegen-synthesized clone thunk, called once per subscriber); delivery rides each thread's `select()` loop over per-endpoint pipes ([TDD-00099](../tdd/TDD-00099.md), [ADR-00309](../adr/ADR-00309.md))<br>• A registered `onmessage` holds its thread's loop alive until `close()` (Node ref semantics)<br>• Works same-thread and across workers<br>• verified on darwin/arm64 and Linux (glibc/arm64, Docker) |
| `MessageChannel` / `MessagePort` | ✅ | • Message type fixed at construction (`new MessageChannel<T>()`, default `number`), symmetric for both ports<br>• A port crosses a worker boundary only whole — as `workerData` or as the entire `postMessage` payload — and is **shared, not neutered**: the sender must stop using a sent port (unsynchronized use from two threads is memory-safe but unordered); the `MessageChannel` pair box itself never crosses<br>• `onmessage` property only (arrow literal); no `on('message')`, no `start()`/`'close'` event, no array payloads via `onmessage`<br>• `close()` leaks two pipe fds; `-mm=manual` leaks per message | • Importable under Node's module name too — `import { MessageChannel/MessagePort/BroadcastChannel } from 'worker_threads'` ([ADR-00431](../adr/ADR-00431.md))<br>• One shared endpoint runtime with `BroadcastChannel` (pipe per endpoint, peer-linked halves); a port is drained by whichever thread registered its `onmessage` — no adoption protocol needed when a port moves to a worker ([TDD-00099](../tdd/TDD-00099.md), [ADR-00309](../adr/ADR-00309.md))<br>• `postMessage` into a closed peer silently discards, matching spec<br>• Verified same-thread, port-as-`workerData`, and port-as-`postMessage`-payload round trips (darwin/arm64 and Linux glibc/arm64, Docker) |
| `klain:sync` goroutines, channels, `select` (`go`, `Channel<T>`, `select`) | ✅ | • Channel ops are synchronous blocking (`ch.send(v)`/`ch.receive()`), not `await`; element is a fixed 8-byte slot (number/string/object/boolean)<br>• `select` cases are `ch.recvCase(v => …)` / `ch.sendCase(x, () => …)` / `defaultCase(() => …)`; a recv handler receives the value but not the closed flag (use `for (const v of ch)` range, which ends on close, to detect it)<br>• Fixed goroutine stacks (default 256 KiB, tunable via `KLAINSYNC_STACK_KB`), no overflow guard — deep recursion is UB; true growable/moving stacks are gated on precise stack maps ([TDD-00135](../tdd/TDD-00135.md))<br>• Blocking-syscall P-handoff is a bounded sysmon-driven rescue-M approximation, not full `entersyscall`/`exitsyscall`; a nil (never-constructed) channel isn't expressible — channels are always `new Channel`<br>• Per-iteration capture of a loop `let` directly in a goroutine closure is a pre-existing general closure limitation — pass the value as a function parameter (a `spawn(work)` helper) instead; a `Channel<T>` keeps its type as a parameter/field/return, so channel plumbing splits cleanly across functions and modules ([ADR-00617](../adr/ADR-00617.md))<br>• `send` after `close` and `close` of a closed channel abort the process (Go-panic parity); native-only (compile error under plain `tsc`/Node) | • A Go-style GMP work-stealing scheduler in the embedded C runtime `klainsyncsrc/klainsync.c`: one P + pinned M (pthread) per `GOMAXPROCS`, a global run-queue backstop, half-queue stealing, periodic global-queue poll; blocking channel send/receive parks the *goroutine*, not the OS thread ([TDD-00143](../tdd/TDD-00143.md), [ADR-00541](../adr/ADR-00541.md))<br>• `go(() => void)` spawns; `new Channel<T>(cap)` is an unbuffered rendezvous or buffered ring with `.send`/`.receive`/`.close` and `for (const v of ch)` range; `select(...)` is Go's random-fair select over recv/send cases (`sudog` groups with an atomic winner claim) ([ADR-00543](../adr/ADR-00543.md))<br>• Complete tier-1 cooperative preemption ([ADR-00542](../adr/ADR-00542.md)): a `sysmon` thread flags an over-budget goroutine; the compiler emits `klainsync_safepoint()` at function entry and every loop back-edge (for/while/do-while/for-of/for-in), gated on the resolver's `UsesKlainSync` flag so a program that never imports the module emits and links nothing. Signal-based async preemption is unnecessary given full loop instrumentation<br>• Blocking-call resilience: work-stealing drains a blocked M's goroutines; when all Ms block at once, a bounded rescue M is spawned so the program doesn't deadlock<br>• `LockOSThread` (Go's `runtime.LockOSThread`): a goroutine can bind to its M so it never migrates. The Node event loop / reactor is thread-affine (its `ucontext` connection fibers and per-loop thread-local state can't move OS threads), so `http.listen` run inside a goroutine (`go(() => http.listen(...))`) locks its M at loop entry — a real in-process HTTP server + goroutine-pool load generator in one binary. Preemption is preserved; the locked goroutine resumes on the same M ([ADR-00616](../adr/ADR-00616.md))<br>• Links only when `klain:sync` is imported; `-mm=gc` registers each M and each goroutine stack with Boehm<br>• Validated standalone (rendezvous, 100-goroutine fan-in, close-drain, select, `GOMAXPROCS=1` preemption, all-Ms-blocked rescue) clean under ThreadSanitizer; E2E on darwin/arm64 |
